limitations: Used only the serialized input. Source quotations, curator transcriptions, and finance/research interpretations were not independently verified.
The 2026-05-15 cutoff governs information availability. No target-quarter actuals or remembered target results are used.
These are illustrative analyst assumptions for April–June 2026, not company budget or observed outcomes. Market-to-financial sensitivities are uncalibrated judgments.
Commodity guidance is annual and after tax; its unrecognized quarterly portion, procurement lags, currency exposures, and company demand elasticities are unknown.

Cash, debt repricing, working-capital detail, repurchase plans, and investment commitments are absent. Cash conversion and capex are seasonal; inferred historical diluted shares depend on rounded EPS.
Supplied historical figures contain unresolved USD 1 million arithmetic residuals and inconsistent other-income labels. Contract classification is retained without silently correcting history.

assumptions.basis: Reported YoY sales growth applied to same-quarter-prior-year sales. Retain the frozen control in all scenarios: base moderates Q3's 7% reported growth, including approximately four points of FX, against Q2's 1% and prior-year Q4's 2%. PG07/PG09 affordability and modest real spending offset possible pricing support and PG10 demand resilience; no calibrated net adjustment is justified. Use one joint demand assessment, without adding historical contributions again. Annual organic guidance of 0–4% does not constrain quarterly reported growth.

Gross profit divided by sales. Frozen control bear/base/bull of 0.475/0.490/0.505 already reflects historical compression and Q4 seasonality. Apply incremental reductions of 80/40/20 basis points respectively for the changed commodity outlook in PG06, corroborated by PG08 input and freight inflation. The base assumes some additional cost pressure reaches Q4; bear assumes greater recognition and weaker mitigation, while bull assumes procurement lag and offsets. These magnitudes are illustrative, not measured elasticities. Treat PG06/PG08 as one capped cost adjustment; do not repeat Q3 compression or allocate annual after-tax commodity, tariff, or FX amounts mechanically.

SG&A divided by sales; higher ratios are adverse. Retain all frozen scenarios, anchored near prior-year Q4's 0.2826 and latest Q3's 0.2795. Bear captures expense pressure and weaker absorption; bull captures improved efficiency and absorption. PG10 establishes peer performance but no P&G spending response, so an additional competitive expense charge would be unsupported and could duplicate existing downside.

Quarterly signed interest expense plus interest income plus other income under the contract. Retain the frozen scenarios: base normalizes near prior-year Q4's 166 rather than repeating Q3's 414, which contains other income of 537; Q2's component sum was 55. Bear permits net expense and bull stronger contributions. PG05 supplies policy-rate context but no debt repricing exposure, so no incremental interest adjustment is justified. Other-income recurrence and classification remain uncertain.

Tax expense divided by pretax income; higher rates are adverse. Retain all frozen scenarios. Base lies between prior-year Q4's 0.198 and latest Q3's 0.208, with Q2 at 0.201. Bear/bull reflect unfavorable/favorable tax-mix uncertainty without asserting specific tax events. Eligible market evidence supplies no supported incremental tax change.

Quarterly noncontrolling earnings deducted after tax from total net income. Retain the frozen scenarios: base is near latest Q3's 19, with prior-year Q4 at 11 and Q1 at 31. A larger deduction is adverse to parent earnings. No supplied market evidence supports changing these assumptions or establishes subsidiary profitability.

Quarterly diluted weighted-average EPS denominator. Retain the frozen scenarios, informed by approximate historical denominators declining from 2443 in prior-year Q4 to 2412 in latest Q3. Base assumes a modest further decline; bear/bull use higher/lower denominators, adverse/favorable to EPS. Historical estimates use attributable income divided by rounded EPS and are not reported share counts. No incremental repurchase or financing evidence supports a change.

Quarterly OCF divided by total net income. Retain the frozen scenarios: base weights prior-year Q4's seasonal 1.3748 while tempering toward latest Q3's 1.0238. Bear/bull reflect weaker/stronger cash conversion, affecting cash generation rather than accounting profitability. Input-cost evidence does not quantify working-capital effects, so no additional cash-conversion adjustment is made.

Positive capital expenditure outflow divided by sales. Retain all frozen scenarios, with base near prior-year Q4's 0.0477 and latest Q3's 0.0480. Bear assumes heavier cash investment; bull lower near-term cash intensity. Lower capex favors modeled free cash flow without directly improving earnings or establishing better long-term economics. No eligible investment-plan evidence supports an incremental change.

narrative: The frozen history-only control remains the counterfactual. Only gross margin changes: the joint company-guidance and producer-price signal supports an illustrative incremental cost allowance of 80/40/20 basis points in bear/base/bull. Latest Q3 history is already incorporated and is not counted as a market adjustment. Mixed demand and peer evidence does not justify a net sales-growth change; unrelated drivers remain unchanged. Bear/bull orientation follows parent earnings, EPS, or near-term cash generation as applicable. All values remain within contract bounds. No final financial statements are computed.
